notes.title: Data Privacy Policy Draft — v2.3
notes.content:
Data Privacy Policy — TechFlow AI (v2.3 Draft)
Last updated: 2026-02-25
Status: Under review (publishing with launch on March 15)

Key sections:

1. Data We Collect
- Account data: name, email, company (provided at signup)
- Connected tool data: content metadata from integrations (NOT content itself for free tier)
- Usage data: feature usage, performance metrics, error logs
- Payment data: processed by Stripe (we never see full card numbers)

2. How We Use Data
- Provide and improve the service
- AI processing: on-device for free tier, cloud-optional for pro/enterprise
- Analytics: aggregated, anonymized usage patterns
- NEVER: sell data, train AI on customer data, share with third parties (except sub-processors)

3. Data Storage & Security
- Hosted on AWS (US regions: us-east-1, us-west-2)
- Encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.3)
- SOC2 Type I certified (pending March 2026)
- Employee access: need-to-know basis, logged and audited

4. Data Retention
- Active accounts: data retained while subscription is active
- Cancelled accounts: data deleted within 30 days (or exported on request)
- Logs: 90 days retention, then purged
- Backups: 30-day rolling backups, encrypted

5. User Rights
- Export: download all your data at any time (Settings → Export)
- Delete: request full deletion via support (processed within 72 hours)
- Correction: edit account data directly in settings
- Portability: data export in JSON format

6. Sub-processors
- AWS (infrastructure)
- Stripe (payments)
- Resend (email delivery)
- OpenAI (AI processing — enterprise only, with explicit opt-in)

Changes from v2.2:
- Added OpenAI as sub-processor (new AI features)
- Clarified on-device vs cloud processing distinction
- Added GDPR-specific section (for future EU expansion)
- Updated data retention periods

notes.title: Open Source License Review
notes.content:
Open Source License Compliance Review — Q1 2026
Date: 2026-02-20

Review methodology:
- Scanned all direct and transitive dependencies
- Tool used: FOSSA (free tier)
- Total packages reviewed: 847

License distribution:
- MIT: 612 packages (72%) ✓ (permissive, no concerns)
- Apache 2.0: 134 packages (16%) ✓ (permissive, need NOTICE file)
- BSD (2 or 3 clause): 56 packages (7%) ✓ (permissive)
- ISC: 28 packages (3%) ✓ (permissive)
- MPL 2.0: 8 packages (1%) ⚠️ (weak copyleft — file-level)
- LGPL 2.1: 5 packages (0.6%) ⚠️ (weak copyleft — dynamic linking OK)
- GPL: 0 packages ✓ (no strong copyleft)
- Unknown/Custom: 4 packages (0.5%) ❓ (need manual review)

Concerns:

1. MPL 2.0 packages (8):
- These are file-level copyleft. As long as we don't modify the files, we're fine.
- We don't modify any of these → NO ACTION NEEDED

2. LGPL 2.1 packages (5):
- Dynamic linking is fine. We use these as npm packages (not statically compiled).
- → NO ACTION NEEDED

3. Unknown/Custom (4):
- Reviewed manually:
  - 2 are effectively MIT with slightly different wording → FINE
  - 1 is CC-BY-4.0 (documentation only) → FINE
  - 1 has no license file but README says 'free to use' → LOW RISK
  - Plan: email maintainer of the no-license package to clarify

Compliance actions:
- [x] NOTICE file maintained with Apache 2.0 attributions
- [x] LICENSE file in repo (MIT for our code)
- [x] No GPL contamination
- [ ] Quarterly re-scan scheduled (Q2: May 2026)

Conclusion: Clean bill of health. No licensing risks for commercial use.

notes.title: IP Strategy Discussion with Alex
notes.content:
IP Strategy Meeting — Patent Portfolio
Date: 2026-02-22
Attendees: Elena, Alex

Context: Provisional patent expires November 2026. Need to decide on utility filing.

Discussion:

1. Current provisional: 'Context-Aware AI Productivity System'
- Covers: on-device processing, cross-tool relevance ranking, privacy-preserving AI
- Strength: novel combination of on-device ML + multi-tool context
- Weakness: some prior art in enterprise search (Glean, Google Cloud Search)

2. Should we file utility?
- Cost: $15-20K (filing + prosecution)
- Timeline: 2-4 years to grant
- Benefit: defensive (prevents competitors from patenting similar approach)
- Risk: limited offensive value at our stage (can't afford to litigate)

Alex's view:
- 'The on-device privacy architecture is our real innovation'
- 'Cross-tool search is too broad — prior art concerns'
- 'Let's narrow the claims to privacy-preserving context AI'

Elena's recommendation:
- File utility with narrowed claims (on-device privacy-preserving AI context)
- Budget for 1 more provisional in 2026 (AI-driven notification prioritization)
- Don't file in multiple countries yet (too expensive)
- Revisit international filing before Series B

Decision: Alex to provide updated technical description by June. Elena to work with patent attorney to draft narrowed claims. File by August (3 months before provisional expires).

Action items:
- Alex: technical write-up of on-device AI architecture (June 2026)
- Elena: engage patent attorney for utility drafting (July 2026)

Employment Agreement — Key Terms (Template Summary)

Applies to all new hires. Standard California-compliant terms.

1. At-Will Employment
- Employment is at-will (either party can terminate at any time)
- No guaranteed term of employment
- This overrides any verbal representations

2. Compensation & Benefits
- Per offer letter (incorporated by reference)
- Subject to applicable tax withholding
- Benefits per company policy (may change at company's discretion)

3. Proprietary Information (PIIA)
- All work product belongs to company (work-for-hire)
- Employee assigns all IP created during employment to company
- Confidentiality survives termination (indefinite for trade secrets)
- Reasonable exceptions: prior inventions disclosed on Schedule A

4. Non-Solicitation (NOT non-compete — CA doesn't enforce non-competes)
- 12 months post-termination: cannot solicit employees or customers
- Cannot recruit TechFlow employees to another company
- Does not restrict working for competitors (CA law)

5. Confidentiality
- Company confidential information: trade secrets, financials, customer data, strategies
- Obligation: do not disclose during or after employment
- Return all materials upon termination
- Whistleblower protections preserved per law

6. Dispute Resolution
- Governed by California law
- Mandatory arbitration for individual disputes (JAMS)
- Exceptions: IP enforcement (court), class claims (per law)

7. Background Check
- Standard background check at hire
- Criminal check, employment verification, education verification
- No credit check (not relevant for most roles)

Status: Template reviewed by external employment counsel (December 2025). Valid for California employees.

notes.title: Contractor Agreement Template
notes.content:
Independent Contractor Agreement — Template Summary

Use for: freelancers, consultants, part-time specialists
NOT for: anyone who would be classified as employee under California ABC test

Key terms:

1. Relationship
- Explicitly independent contractor (not employee)
- Contractor controls manner and means of work
- No benefits, no withholding (1099 recipient)
- Company cannot set schedule or require on-site

2. Scope of Work
- Defined in Exhibit A (specific project or deliverables)
- Not open-ended — must have defined scope/term
- Renewals require new SOW

3. Compensation
- Flat fee or hourly rate (per SOW)
- Invoicing: monthly, net-15 payment
- No overtime, no benefits, no equity (unless separately granted)

4. IP Assignment
- All work product created under agreement assigned to company
- Contractor retains pre-existing IP (with license to company if used)
- Moral rights waived (to extent permitted)

5. Confidentiality
- Standard NDA terms (mutual)
- Contractor may not disclose company information
- Survives termination

6. Term & Termination
- Per SOW (project-based or time-based)
- Either party can terminate with 14 days written notice
- Immediate termination for material breach

California ABC Test Warning:
- A: Contractor free from control and direction
- B: Work performed is outside company's usual business OR at contractor's own location
- C: Contractor has independently established trade/business

Risk areas: designers, engineers, and writers who work >20 hrs/week exclusively for us could be misclassified. Elena reviews all contractor arrangements >$5K/month.

notes.content:
Non-Disclosure Agreement — Standard Template

Type: Mutual NDA (both parties share confidential information)
Term: 2 years from signing (confidentiality obligations survive 3 years)

Definition of Confidential Information:
- Technical: source code, algorithms, system architecture, databases
- Business: financials, pricing, customer lists, strategies, forecasts
- People: employee data, compensation, performance
- Legal: contracts, IP filings, legal opinions

Exclusions (standard):
- Publicly available information
- Information known prior to disclosure
- Independently developed without reference to confidential info
- Compelled disclosure by law (with notice)

Obligations:
- Use only for intended purpose (evaluation, partnership, employment)
- Protect with reasonable care (at least same as own confidential info)
- Limit access to need-to-know individuals
- Return or destroy upon request or termination

Use cases:
- Candidates interviewing (sign before technical interviews)
- Potential partners (sign before product demo/API access)
- Investors (sign before due diligence — though most VCs won't sign)
- Vendors (sign before sharing technical requirements)

Signed NDAs on file: 23
- Employees: 11/14 (need Jake, Tom, Derek — chasing)
- Candidates: 8 (from interview process)
- Vendors: 4 (AWS, Vanta, NCC Group, accounting firm)

Note: VCs (Dana, Victor) did NOT sign NDAs — industry standard. They see too many deals.

- Acceleration: double-trigger (change of control + termination/demotion)

Termination provisions:
- Voluntary resignation: 90-day exercise window
- Termination without cause: 90-day exercise window
- Termination for cause: immediate forfeiture of all unvested AND vested but unexercised
- Death/disability: 12-month exercise window

Change of Control:
- Single trigger: not applicable (unvested does NOT auto-accelerate on acquisition)
- Double trigger: if acquired AND employee terminated/demoted within 12 months, 100% acceleration
- This protects employees while not over-committing the buyer

ISO limits:
- $100K aggregate FMV vesting per year (excess becomes NSO)
- Only for US employees
- Non-employees (contractors): NSO only

notes.title: Legal FAQ for Team
notes.content:
Legal FAQ — For TechFlow Team
Maintained by: Elena Park | Last updated: March 2026

Q: Can I talk to journalists about TechFlow?
A: All press inquiries go to Nina. Do not comment on: funding, revenue, customer names, or unreleased features. You can share your personal title and general enthusiasm.

Q: Can I share product screenshots on social media?
A: Yes for publicly available features (after launch). Never share: internal dashboards, customer data, unreleased features, or internal communications.

Q: What if a customer asks me to sign something?
A: NEVER sign anything on behalf of the company. Route all contracts, NDAs, letters of intent, or any binding document to Elena.

Q: Can I use open source code in our product?
A: Yes for MIT, Apache 2.0, BSD licenses. Check with Elena before using: GPL, AGPL, SSPL, or any 'copyleft' license. When in doubt, ask.

Q: What if I accidentally see something confidential (salary, customer data)?
A: Don't share it. Don't screenshot it. Report the access issue to whoever manages that system. No one will be in trouble for reporting.

Q: Can I work on side projects?
A: Yes, as long as they: (1) don't compete with TechFlow, (2) don't use company resources or time, (3) don't use confidential information. Disclose to Alex/Sarah if there's any overlap.

Q: What should I do if I receive a legal threat or subpoena?
A: Immediately forward to Elena. Do not respond, do not discuss with anyone else, do not delete anything.

Q: Can I expense legal costs for my own issues?
A: No. Company expenses are for company business only.

Q: Where do I find contract templates?
A: Shared drive → Legal → Templates. NDA, PIIA, offer letter, contractor agreement. Don't modify without Elena's review.

Contact: elena@techflow.ai or #legal on Slack

notes.title: Acme Corp Contract — Redline Summary
notes.content:
Acme Corp Enterprise Contract — Redline Analysis
Received: February 25, 2026
Reviewer: Elena Park

Their redlines (changes they want):

1. Liability cap: They want 24 months of fees (we offered 12 months)
   My analysis: Common ask from larger companies. 12 months is industry standard.
   Recommendation: Compromise at 18 months. Maximum I'd accept: 24 months given deal size.
   Status: Counter-proposed 18 months — awaiting response.

2. Data deletion: They want 15 days (we offer 30 days)
   My analysis: 15 days is aggressive but doable technically.
   Recommendation: Accept. Shows good faith, and faster deletion is actually better for our risk.
   Status: ACCEPTED.

3. Indemnification: They want mutual indemnification for IP infringement
   My analysis: Standard. We should indemnify them for IP claims arising from our product.
   Recommendation: Accept mutual indemnification with standard carve-outs.
   Status: ACCEPTED with carve-outs (their modifications void indemnity).

4. SLA: They want 99.99% (we offer 99.9%)
   My analysis: 99.99% is 52 minutes of downtime per YEAR. Very aggressive.
   Recommendation: Hold at 99.9%. We cannot guarantee four-nines today.
   Status: Counter-proposed 99.9% with enhanced credits. Awaiting response.

5. Audit rights: They want right to audit our security practices annually
   My analysis: Common for enterprise. Controlled audit rights are fine.
   Recommendation: Accept with limitations (30-day notice, during business hours, at their cost, max 1 per year).
   Status: ACCEPTED with limitations.

6. Insurance: They want us to carry $5M E&O insurance
   My analysis: We have $1M. $5M is expensive but possible.
   Recommendation: Accept but increase insurance gradually. Ask for 6-month grace period.
   Status: Counter-proposed $2M with commitment to $5M within 12 months.

Overall assessment:
- Their asks are reasonable for a $100K enterprise deal
- No deal-breakers
- Expect 1 more round of back-and-forth
- Target: signed by March 15-20

Rachel's note: 'Don't let legal terms delay this deal. This is our biggest contract.'

notes.title: Data Retention Policy — Draft
notes.content:
Data Retention Policy — TechFlow AI (DRAFT)
Version: 1.0 | Status: Draft for SOC2
Owner: Elena Park

Purpose: Define how long TechFlow retains different types of data.

1. Customer data (connected tool content)
- Active subscription: retained while active
- Cancelled subscription: retained 30 days for export, then deleted
- Explicit deletion request: processed within 72 hours
- Backups: retained 30 days after primary deletion (then purged)

2. Account data (name, email, preferences)
- Active: retained while active
- Cancelled: retained 30 days, then anonymized (keep aggregate stats)
- Legal hold: retained indefinitely if subject to legal proceedings

3. Usage analytics
- Identifiable: retained 90 days (for product improvement)
- Anonymized/aggregated: retained indefinitely (for trend analysis)
- Opt-out: users can opt out of identifiable analytics

4. System logs
- Application logs: 90 days
- Security logs (access, authentication): 1 year
- Audit logs (SOC2 relevant): 3 years
- Error logs: 30 days

5. Employee data
- Current employees: retained during employment
- Former employees: retained per California law (4 years for payroll)
- Candidates (not hired): retained 3 years (per EEOC guidance)

6. Financial records
- Invoices, contracts, receipts: 7 years (IRS requirement)
- Tax returns: 7 years
- Board minutes: permanent

7. Legal documents
- Contracts: 7 years post-expiration
- NDAs: 7 years post-termination
- IP filings: permanent

Deletion procedures:
- Automated: retention engine purges expired data monthly
- Manual: privacy team (Elena) reviews deletion queue weekly
- Verification: quarterly audit of retention compliance
- Documentation: deletion certificates for enterprise customers on request

Exceptions:
- Legal hold overrides all retention periods
- Regulatory requirements may extend retention
- Customer contracts may specify custom retention
